cases.sentence: За здоровье тайного ___ Иоганна фон Гёте.
cases.translation: To the health of the privy councillor Johann von Goethe.
cases.explain: «За здоровье» is «за» plus the genitive of the noun здоровье, and the person whose health it is follows in the genitive too: здоровье (кого?) советника.

cases.translation: Allow me to ask you one trifling question.
cases.explain: «Вопрос» is the direct object of «задать», so it stands in the accusative; the noun is inanimate, so the accusative looks like the nominative.

cases.sentence: Отчего это в ___ у вас столько грусти?
cases.translation: Why is there so much sadness in your eyes?
cases.explain: «В» answering «где?» (a location, not a direction) takes the prepositional case: в глазах.

cases.sentence: Отчего это в глазах у вас столько ___?
cases.translation: Why is there so much sadness in your eyes?
cases.explain: Quantity words like «столько» govern the genitive, so грусть becomes грусти.

cases.translation: And the sadness comes from a woman.
cases.explain: Here грусть is the subject of the clause (what comes from a woman), so it stands in the nominative.

cases.translation: In the morning — a revaluation of all these values.
cases.explain: The verbal noun «переоценка» takes its object in the genitive, exactly as «переоценка ценностей».

cases.sentence: Ни о чем она не заботится так рьяно, как о ___.
cases.translation: There is nothing she cares about so zealously as balance.
cases.explain: «Заботиться о ком/чём» uses the preposition «о» with the prepositional case: о равновесии.

cases.sentence: Потому что в расчет не принимает ___!
cases.translation: Because it does not take a woman into account!
cases.explain: «Принимать в расчёт» is transitive and its object is accusative; here the speaker keeps the accusative бабу even after «не».

cases.sentence: Если б баба не была ___, лемма не была бы леммой.
cases.translation: If a woman were not a woman, the lemma would not be a lemma.
cases.explain: A predicate noun after быть in the past or conditional goes into the instrumental — compare «лемма не была бы леммой» in the same sentence.

cases.sentence: Нельзя же ехать к ___ и не пить!
cases.translation: You can't travel to a woman and not drink!
cases.explain: The preposition «к» (motion towards a person) always governs the dative: к бабе.

reading.ru: За здоровье тайного советника Иоганна фон Гёте.
reading.question: Whose health is the toast drunk to at the start of the chapter?
options: The privy councillor Johann von Goethe
reading.correct: The privy councillor Johann von Goethe
reading.explain: The company raises the drink to Goethe, given his official title of privy councillor.

reading.ru: Разве можно грустить, имея такие познания!
reading.question: Why does the black-moustached man find Venichka's sadness surprising?
options: Because a man with such learning ought not to be sad
Because Venichka is going to Petushki
Because everyone else on the train is sad
Because Venichka has just been paid
reading.correct: Because a man with such learning ought not to be sad
reading.explain: He argues that someone with such knowledge has no business being sad.

reading.ru: Можно подумать – вы с утра ничего не пили!
reading.question: What does the black-moustached man say Venichka looks like?
options: Like someone who has not drunk anything since morning
Like someone who has drunk far too much
Like someone who has just woken up
Like someone who has lost his ticket
reading.correct: Like someone who has not drunk anything since morning
reading.explain: He says one might think Venichka had drunk nothing all morning.

reading.ru: Это просто замутненность глаз…
reading.question: How does Venichka himself explain the look in his eyes?
options: As a mere cloudiness of the eyes
As the effect of the diagram
reading.correct: As a mere cloudiness of the eyes
reading.explain: He denies it is sadness and calls it simply a cloudiness of the eyes, adding that he has had a little to drink.

reading.ru: Вы как Гёте!
reading.question: Whom does the black-moustached man compare Venichka to?
reading.correct: Goethe
reading.explain: He says Venichka, like Goethe, refutes everything — including his lemma.

reading.ru: И черноусый изобразил на бумажке такую вот хреновину.
reading.question: How does the black-moustached man present his lemma to the others?
options: He draws a diagram on a scrap of paper
He recites it from memory in verse
He reads it out of a notebook
He acts it out with the suitcase
reading.correct: He draws a diagram on a scrap of paper
reading.explain: He sketches a curve on a bit of paper and then explains what its lines mean.

reading.ru: Наивысшая точка кривой – момент засыпания, наинизшая – пробуждения с похмелья…
reading.question: What does the highest point of the curve stand for?
options: The moment of waking up with a hangover
reading.correct: The moment of falling asleep
reading.explain: The peak is the moment of falling asleep and the lowest point is waking up hung over.

reading.ru: Это же голая зеркальность!
reading.question: What does the black-moustached man call the pattern his curve shows?
reading.correct: Naked mirror symmetry
reading.explain: He insists the evening and the morning mirror each other exactly.

reading.ru: Не знаю, нравственна ли это забота, но она строго геометрична!
reading.question: How does he describe nature's concern for balance?
options: He is unsure whether it is moral, but it is strictly geometrical
He calls it both moral and merciful
He says it applies only to drinkers
reading.correct: He is unsure whether it is moral, but it is strictly geometrical
reading.explain: He says nature cares for nothing so zealously as balance, and that this care is strictly geometrical.

reading.ru: Вечером – бесстрашие, даже если и есть причина бояться, бесстрашие и недооценка всех ценностей.
reading.question: According to the lemma, what characterises the evening?
options: Fearlessness and an undervaluing of all values
Fear and a revaluation of all values
A longing for the ideal only
reading.correct: Fearlessness and an undervaluing of all values
reading.explain: The evening brings fearlessness; the morning brings the opposite, a revaluation turning into groundless fear.

reading.ru: Она – всеобща и к каждому применима.
reading.question: What does the black-moustached man claim about his cherished lemma?
options: That it is universal and applies to everyone
That it applies only to men with moustaches
That it applies only to Goethe
That it is impossible to prove
reading.correct: That it is universal and applies to everyone
reading.explain: He presents it as universal — which is exactly why Venichka and the Decembrist ask why it is called a lemma at all.

reading.ru: Потому что в расчет не принимает бабу!
reading.question: Why, in his own words, is it still only a lemma?
options: Because it does not take women into account
Because it has never been written down
Because it only works on trains
reading.correct: Because it does not take women into account
reading.explain: It accounts for a person in the pure state, but not for a woman.

reading.ru: С появлением бабы нарушается всякая зеркальность.
reading.question: What destroys the mirror symmetry of the lemma?
options: A second glass in the morning
The arrival of the ticket inspector
reading.correct: The appearance of a woman
reading.explain: As soon as a woman appears, the neat symmetry between evening and morning breaks down.

reading.ru: «Плохих баб нет, только леммы одни бывают плохие…»
reading.question: What does one of the voices in the general uproar claim?
options: That there are no bad women, only bad lemmas
That there are no good lemmas at all
That bad women are the most useful ones
reading.correct: That there are no bad women, only bad lemmas
reading.explain: In the burst of shouting someone turns the question round and blames the lemmas instead of the women.

reading.ru: Все-таки, я считаю: тридцать самых плохих баб лучше, чем одна, хоть и самая хорошая…
reading.question: What is the Decembrist's own view of the matter?
options: Thirty of the worst women are better than one, even the very best
One good woman is worth all thirty
Neither good nor bad women are needed
reading.correct: Thirty of the worst women are better than one, even the very best
reading.explain: He boasts of having thirty women and prefers quantity to quality.

reading.ru: Разговор о бабе идет, а не об усах!
reading.question: What does the black-moustached man object to in the Decembrist's argument?
options: That the conversation is about women, not about moustaches
That thirty is too small a number
That the Decembrist has no moustache
reading.correct: That the conversation is about women, not about moustaches
reading.explain: He protests at the moustaches being dragged in, and the Decembrist answers that without moustaches there would be no conversation at all.

reading.ru: А зверобой стоит 2.62.
reading.question: How much does a bottle of zveroboy cost, by Venichka's reckoning?
reading.explain: Thirty empties at twelve kopecks make 3.60, while the bottle itself costs 2.62.

reading.ru: Отчего Пушкин умер, они еще не знают, а это – уже знают.
reading.question: What does Venichka say children already know?
options: The prices, though not yet why Pushkin died
Why Pushkin died, though not the prices
How to swap empties for a bottle
reading.correct: The prices, though not yet why Pushkin died
reading.explain: He offers it as proof that the arithmetic of empties and bottles is common knowledge.

reading.ru: А хорошая баба – берет у вас плохую посуду, а взамен дает хорошую.
reading.question: What, according to Venichka, makes the woman behind the shop counter a good one?
options: She takes your bad empties and gives good bottles in return
She always gives the change back
She never charges for the bottle
She keeps the shop open at dawn
reading.correct: She takes your bad empties and gives good bottles in return
reading.explain: A bad woman would not take the empties at all; a good one accepts them and gives a full bottle back, so she must be honoured.

reading.ru: «Мерило всякой цивилизации – способ отношения к женщине».
reading.question: What saying of Maxim Gorky does Venichka quote?
options: That the measure of any civilisation is the way it treats women
That a man must not drink before evening
That Capri is the finest place on earth
reading.correct: That the measure of any civilisation is the way it treats women
reading.explain: He quotes it as his justification for leaving the change with the shop woman.

reading.ru: Так и ухожу, без всякой сдачи.
reading.question: What does Venichka do about the change in his vision of the shop?
options: He leaves without taking any change
He buys a second bottle with it
He gives it to the Decembrist
reading.correct: He leaves without taking any change
reading.explain: The imagined Gorky on Capri wags a finger at him not to take the change, and he obeys, grumbling.

reading.ru: Хорошему человеку плохая баба иногда прямо необходима бывает.
reading.question: How does Venichka answer the Decembrist's question about bad women?
options: A good man sometimes absolutely needs a bad woman
Bad women should always be avoided
Only thirty bad women are of any use
Bad women exist only in lemmas
reading.correct: A good man sometimes absolutely needs a bad woman
reading.explain: He then tells how such a woman raised him from the coffin he had lain in for four years.

reading.ru: Подошла ко гробу и говорит: «Талифа куми».
reading.question: What did the woman say when she came up to Venichka's coffin?
reading.correct: «Talitha koum»
reading.explain: He glosses the words as 'I say to you, arise and walk' — and says he got up and went.

reading.ru: И вот уж три месяца хожу замутненный…
reading.question: How long has Venichka been walking about in his clouded state?
reading.correct: Three months
reading.explain: He dates his cloudiness from the moment the woman raised him twelve weeks earlier.

reading.ru: У нас тут прямо как у Тургенева: все сидят и спорят про любовь…
reading.question: What comparison does the Decembrist make about the company in the carriage?
options: That they are like characters in Turgenev, sitting and arguing about love
That they are like Goethe's readers
That they are like children in a shop
That they are like Gorky on Capri
reading.correct: That they are like characters in Turgenev, sitting and arguing about love
reading.explain: Delighted at how cultivated they all are, he proposes that everyone tell a story, as in Turgenev.

reading.ru: Даже старый Митрич – и тот сказал: «Давайте!..»
reading.question: How does the chapter end?
options: Even old Mitrich agrees to the storytelling
Mitrich alone refuses to join in
reading.correct: Even old Mitrich agrees to the storytelling
reading.explain: The whole company takes up the Decembrist's proposal, old Mitrich included.

highlight.question: Which sentence says that Venichka looks as though he has not had anything to drink all morning?
sentences: – А… разрешите вам задать один пустяшный вопрос, – сказал черноусый сквозь усы и сквозь бутерброд в усах: он опять обращался только ко мне.
– Разрешите спросить: отчего это в глазах у вас столько грусти?..
Разве можно грустить, имея такие познания!
Можно подумать – вы с утра ничего не пили!
highlight.explain: Only the last sentence draws the conclusion that Venichka has drunk nothing since morning.

highlight.question: Which sentence is Venichka's admission that he has had a little to drink?
sentences: – Как, то есть, ничего!
И разве это грусть?
Это просто замутненность глаз…
Я просто немного поддал…
highlight.explain: The final sentence is where he concedes he has drunk a bit, after denying that his look is sadness.

highlight.question: Which sentence explains what the highest and lowest points of the drawn curve mean?
sentences: И черноусый изобразил на бумажке такую вот хреновину.
И объяснил: горизонтальная линия – это линия обычной трезвости, повседневная линия.
Наивысшая точка кривой – момент засыпания, наинизшая – пробуждения с похмелья…
highlight.explain: The last sentence names the peak as falling asleep and the trough as waking with a hangover, while the previous one describes only the horizontal line.

highlight.question: Which sentence claims that it is the lemmas, not the women, that can be bad?
sentences: Враз заговорили все.
«Да что такое вообще лемма?»
«И что такое – плохая баба?»
«Плохих баб нет, только леммы одни бывают плохие…»
highlight.explain: The last shouted remark turns the question round and blames the lemmas.

highlight.question: Which sentence states the Decembrist's conclusion about thirty bad women against one good one?
sentences: – У меня, например, – сказал декабрист, – у меня тридцать баб, и одна чище другой, хоть и усов у меня нет.
А у вас, допустим, усы и одна хорошая баба.
Все-таки, я считаю: тридцать самых плохих баб лучше, чем одна, хоть и самая хорошая…
highlight.explain: The first two sentences only set out the two situations; the third gives his verdict.

highlight.question: Which sentence says that children do not yet know why Pushkin died but do already know this?
sentences: – Да иначе кто ж вам обменяет!
Тридцать на двенадцать – это 3.60.
А зверобой стоит 2.62.
Это и дети знают.
Отчего Пушкин умер, они еще не знают, а это – уже знают.
А все-таки никакой сдачи.
3.60, конечно, хорошо, это лучше, чем 2.62, но все-таки сдачи не берешь, потому что за витриной стоит хорошая баба, а хорошую бабу надо уважить…
highlight.explain: Pushkin's death is mentioned in only one sentence, the one contrasting what children do and do not know.

highlight.question: Which sentence describes what a good woman does with the bad empties you bring her?
sentences: – Да тем и хороша, что плохая вообще бы посуду у вас не взяла.
А хорошая баба – берет у вас плохую посуду, а взамен дает хорошую.
И поэтому надо уважить…
Для чего вообще на свете баба?
highlight.explain: The second sentence is the one that says she takes the bad empties and gives good ones in exchange.

highlight.question: Which sentence gives the translation of the words spoken over the coffin?
sentences: – Вот-вот!
Подошла ко гробу и говорит: «Талифа куми».
Это значит в переводе с древнежидовского: «Тебе говорю – встань и ходи».
И что ж вы думаете?
Встал – и пошел.
И вот уж три месяца хожу замутненный…
highlight.explain: The third sentence renders «Талифа куми» into Russian, while the second only quotes it.
